To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the TA provided by the NTTAC to SOC sites is effective in supporting SOC development, that NTTAC’s TA model is flexible enough to respond to the changing needs of SOC sites, and that NTTAC is responsive to its TA recipients’ feedback and needs.

the NTTAC process evaluation results suggest that it is feasible to develop TA methods based on the needs and goals of the TA recipients (SOC grantees), and that the TA methods can be used to improve SOC development and behavioral service delivery.
the NTTAC process evaluation found that TA dosage matched need, TA recipients were satisfied with the TA they received, and SOC development indicators improved over time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an evidence-based TA model for SOC.
the question: “What does it take to provide TA that is effective in promoting the development of systems of care?”
the question, “How does the NTTAC TA model work?” and we have found that the NTTAC model is effective in supporting SOC development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NTTAC process evaluation data provide support for the effectiveness of NTTAC in supporting SOC development.

the process evaluation of the NTTAC for Child, Youth and Family Mental Health found that TA dosage matched need and goals of the TA recipients, that overall levels of satisfaction was high, and that TA content was generally in alignment with need.
the NTTAC process evaluation results suggest that it is indeed possible to develop and provide TA methods that reflect recipients’ goals and positively impact SOC development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a TA model that is responsive to the goals of TA recipients, that recipients are satisfied with the TA, and that TA recipients are experiencing positive change in their systems of care.
the NTTAC model is a promising, effective model of TA delivery that is responsive to the needs of TA recipients. (author abstract)
we have developed and refined a process to develop an evidence-based TA model, and that the process is effective in supporting the development of SOC for children, youth, and their families with SED.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible and important to develop and implement a TA model that is responsive to the needs and goals of the TA recipients, and that is based on evidence.
the NTTAC TA approach is effective and can be adapted to support other TA providers and TA recipient sites.
the process evaluation approach we describe here is an important step toward developing a more robust evidence base on the impact of TA.
